newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady to firmer, crude helps.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady to firmer, crude helps.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady to firmer on Tuesday, traders said.

Gas oil prices were steady to firmer with recent trade into Spain at around cif high quites +$3 pegging outright prices for tight diesel supplies higher while 0.2 sulphur prices held steady in balanced trade.
Traders said buying for heating oil cargoes was slower on Tuesday with demand from the east Med mostly covered.
Values for Russian cargoes were pegged around high cif quotes +$3.50 a tonne cif Med and fob Italian Islands material around high fob quotes +$4 a tonne.
Diesel cargoes talked steady around benchmark quotes +$3 cif Med following trade into Spain at the level on Tuesday.
High sulphur fuel oil continued strong with low avails forcing Mediterranean buyers to look in NWE for cargoes.
A 30,000-tonne cargo of 380 CST bunker M-100 material was picked up by a Spanish refiner at $95 cif Las Palmas from an indenpendent European trader.
"They've been bidding $92/$93 for the past few days but these numbers don't work to the Med," the seller said.
Others these prices would be hard to translate into Augusta-based prices.
But a trader with a major refiner said with avails low and demand strong, high sulphur fob cracked was stronger in the Med, in the $80/$82 mark.
"It seems with demand strong in the Med and with avails in the north, stuff may start moving down from the north to the Med," one trader said.
Low sulphur fuel was quiet but two or three Russian pieces were heard on offer but no indication of prices was available.
There was wide market speculation about the price a Med buyer paid for a cargo in the north on Monday, with many saying it was $102 cif, $2 lower than another it picked up last week.
North African naphtha continued to be of interest to Asian buyers and levels were holding around fob high quotes +$2-3, dealers said. Gasoline levels were also steady, although demand fairly slow.
